A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same geometry-aware video-generation method. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated and real-world video-generation results, manipulation success rates in Tables 1–2, and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds multi-task real-world results, a policy baseline, resource measurements, tracking-error analysis, and three-view evaluation.

M1.justification: The trained architecture, diffusion losses, cross-attention mechanism, and FoundationPose pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 adds an inference extension that handles additional views through separate forward passes pairing each new view with the reference view, without retraining.

E1.justification: Real-world coverage expands from PutSpatulaOnTable alone to also include AddOrangeSlicesToBowl, PutCupOnSaucer, and TwistCapOffBottle (Section 4.1). The three simulation tasks remain. Appendix A.7 additionally evaluates generation from three unseen viewpoints.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds DP3, conditioned on colored global point clouds, alongside Dreamitate and Diffusion Policy, renamed DP. Table 1 retains the same generation comparators: the cross-attention ablation, 4D Gaussian using Shape of Motion, SVD, and SVD with multi-view attention.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises simulation demonstration counts from 25/22/20 to 25 per task while retaining the 12-training-view/4-test-view split. Real-world training changes from five spatula demonstrations to 20 demonstrations per task with multi-task fine-tuning for approximately 15,000 steps. Appendices add ground-truth RGB-D tracking controls with per-action MSE and a three-view evaluation. Unchanged simulation scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained cross-attention ablation, v2 adds comparative resource analysis in Table 3, FoundationPose evaluation on ground-truth RGB-D with error curves and high-error examples in Appendix A.6/Figure 13, and a three-view scalability study in Appendix A.7/Table 4. These investigate computational costs, tracking failures, and scaling beyond two views.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, variability across training runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 30 policy evaluations per task are retained. The new tracking MSE curves report prediction errors without introducing statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains simulation values but replaces single-task real-world results with multi-task results; OURS mIoU changes from 0.58 to 0.56 under different data conditions. Table 2 revises Dreamitate's Task 3/average from 0.00/0.09 to 0.10/0.12 and adds DP3. Tables 3–4 and Figure 13 add resource, three-view, and tracking outcomes. DP3's reported 0.25 average is inconsistent with its task scores of 0.23, 0.27, and 0.00.

T1.justification: The pointmap definitions, diffusion objectives in Equations 1–3, and gripper-weighted loss in Appendix A.1/Equation 4 are mathematically unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about geometric supervision, temporally and spatially consistent generation, novel viewpoints without camera-pose inputs, and tracker-derived manipulation policies. Specifying a single RGB-D image per view clarifies an input configuration already documented in v1 Appendix A.1.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of deployment constraints: Section 4.3 attributes DP3's remaining failures to small-object grasping, Appendix A.3 discusses the RGB-D computation tradeoff and hierarchical planning, and Appendix A.7 discusses linear inference costs with additional views. Section 5 explicitly identifies closed-loop planning difficulties but drops the clean-depth assumption statement. Appendix A.6's small-error interpretation does not reconcile Figure 13's apple-task frame labelled MSE 2.5124.

D1.justification: v2 discloses task-specific gripper thresholds of 0.10/0.06/0.12 m, execution of the first six DP actions from a 16-step prediction, DP3 point-cloud aggregation, and comparative memory and parameter counts. Section 8 adds a promise to release code, datasets, and pretrained models upon acceptance; it does not establish current availability. Existing optimizer, hardware, and sampler details remain.

R1.justification: Targeted references are added for DP3, ORV, VGGT, Fast3R, CV-VAE, and faster generation or hierarchical planning. The central positioning relative to SVD, DUSt3R, and object-centric 4D generation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and experimental prose, condenses task descriptions, changes citations to author–year format, and subdivides the dataset appendix. It adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements, partly replacing the broader-impact discussion. The main scientific narrative and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and substantially expands visual presentation. The simulation-task montage moves from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 6. The real-world display becomes multi-task, with additional task and sequence figures. Tables 3–4 and tracking-error Figure 13 are new; retained simulation comparisons are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The four-task real-world evaluation and RGB-D policy comparator strengthen evidence beyond v1's five real-world demonstrations and RGB-based policy baselines. Added implementation details and resource measurements improve transparency. These gains are limited by unchanged simulation scores despite revised sample counts, the inconsistent DP3 average in Table 2, and the unexplained MSE 2.5124 example in Figure 13 despite Appendix A.6 describing only much smaller notable errors.
